title: Down Headlong from Their Native Skies
description: Down Headlong from Their Native Skies in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 96, headed “Distinguishing love; or, Angels punished and men saved”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Down head-long from their na-tive skies The re-bel an-gels fell, And thun-der-bolts of fla-ming wrath Pur-su'd them deep to hell.

lines: Down headlong from their native skies
Down from the top of earthly bliss
And Jesus stoop'd beneath the grave
Must angels sink for ever down,
While God forsakes his shining throne
O for this love let earth and skies
And the full choir of human tongues

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
